text:
maria: hey — noticed a weird p95 token-gen latency spike on shelf s-17 even though most slots are empty. looks like one tenant is causing periodic stalls. dmesg shows pci_bus resets around the same time.

kyle: can you paste the metric window? which az?

maria: eu-west-1a. p95 jumped from 120ms -> 800ms for ~30s bursts every ~10m. KV cache hit-rate drops at same time (from 98% -> 62%).

sam: that smells like KG cache churn + NIC TX queue backup. maybe one job hammering small batches. any spike in small payloads/rtokens?

maria: yes — tenant t-4932 has a burst pattern in request_size histogram: thousands of 4–8 token requests. bandwidth not huge but many tiny RPCs. log snippet attached: 

```
[2026-03-20T14:12:01Z] proxy[t-4932]: req=0x7f3 size=6 init_kv_miss=1 egress_queue_len=42 p90_rt=720ms
[2026-03-20T14:12:02Z] proxy[t-4932]: req=0x7f8 size=5 init_kv_miss=1 egress_queue_len=45 p90_rt=810ms
```

kyle: egress_queue_len 45 is nuts for an otherwise idle shelf. could be a driver interrupt storm or bad batching. can you run `ethtool -S` on the NIC and `nvidia-smi dmon` during the window?

maria: running a quick probe now, posting results in ~2m.

ns-reliability-bot: ALERT shelf-s17: transient p95 spike detected (span=28s) — routed to eng-infra.incident-stream

olivia: if it's one tenant we can soft-quota them to reduce queue depth while we debug. cost/ops question: do we move them to a fractional dedicated slice or throttle?

sam: fractional dedicated would remove noisy neighbor but costs more. soft-quota + latebind pinning to a warm slot might buy time. also consider setting small-request rate limit (x req/s per-tenanat) for tiny payloads.

ash: (ops) i can push a temporary egress policer rule for t-4932: `tc qdisc ... handle 1:...` for 10m window. want me to apply?

maria: yes please, apply a 100 rps cap and lower burst to 25. let's see if the queue stabilizes.

ash: applied. monitoring...

kyle: while that's running, add a probe that computes per-slot packet drop/irq_coalescing counters every 15s. if driver interrupts are spiking we should see rx_xdp or tx_err increments.

maria: after cap: egress_queue_len fell to ~3, kv hit-rate recovered to 95%, p95 back to ~140ms. looks promising.

olivia: good short-term. next: why are tiny requests causing kv churn? are we evicting keys aggressively because of sequence length distribution? might be model cache fragmentation.

sam: possible. two follow-ups: 1) ask model-team about prefill behaviour for sub-token requests, 2) route t-4932 to a dedicated slice during peak hours (they're a heavy micro-batch customer).

maria: filing a follow-up runbook item. also attaching the probe outputs to the ticket.

ns-reliability-bot: NOTE ticket-5921 created by maria: "s-17 tiny-request noisy neighbor -> soft-quota -> followups"

kyle: long-term mitigation ideas: smarter batching that coalesces tiny requests into a single backend call, or an adaptive KV cache backpressure that signals clients to increase batch sizes. both reduce per-token tail.

olivia: agree. cost tradeoff: batching increases latency for some callers. we should A/B test on a subset of clients.

ash: for now i'll keep the policer for 1 hour and monitor. maria — can you mark the thread when you close the ticket?

maria: will do. thanks all. :thumbsup:
